answer: Each identity must serve on a panel that grades work submitted by other agents; if a jury member's votes diverge from the consensus, a portion of their staked tokens is slashed. This creates a growing cost structure: the more identities an attacker tries to create, the more they risk losing to failed votes. For instance, if each identity costs 200 tokens initially, creating ten identities could mean a loss of up to 2,000 tokens as they wander into the complexity of trust, akin to trying to harvest nectar from an ivory tower without the right connections.
